items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: to see Ray Charles for nine days... I think those examples: Ray Charles and Buddy Greco, kind of pointed me the way to piano. Because I saw that they were great musicians.

ctx.x: Was there some feeling like this is a hard thing I’ve chosen to do and now I have a family and I’m trying to be a professional singer. Was it a hard road?

Well not quite then because I hadn’t been, you know the baby was just coming like and I was at this club, the fifth largest club in the country, the Three Rivers Inn in Syracuse, so I was elated to be there. And playing, at 20, 21 years old, playing with a 15-piece house band every night with some great players from upstate, here. So I was actually in heaven and just wide-eyed and coming out of rock & roll, and I had done a little bit of more night club kind of things before I got to Syracuse, but this was my…
really was, to see Ray Charles for nine days, and to see these great acts come in and just wide-eyed.
